newsitem.title: CHINA: China to purchase 70,000 T of rubber from states.
newsitem.headline: China to purchase 70,000 T of rubber from states.

text.p: The Chinese government plans to buy 70,000 tonnes of natural rubber at 14,500 yuan per tonne from three provinces, the China Securities newspaper said on Wednesday.
Of the total, 30,000 tonnes would be alloted to state reserves and 40,000 tonnes would be redistributed by the Ministry of Chemical Industry to state enterprises, it said.
The price would be allowed a 15 percent upward or downward fluctuation, it said.

The southern provinces of Hainan and Guangdong were expected to supply 50,000 tonnes and 2,000 tonnes of natural rubber, respectively, and the southwestern province of Yunnan would supply 18,000 tonnes, it said.

Hainan's natural rubber production in 1996 could slip due to cold weather and typhoons, the newspaper said. The province produces about 200,000 tonnes a year, or 60 percent of national output. Domestic natural rubber production meets about half of China's rubber demand, it said.
China's rubber inventories, already at high levels, were likely to climb in the third quarter of 1996 due to strong domestic production and imports, it added.
